recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No current FHIR core edit is required for FHIR-22505; future work should not rewrite historical release bundles or intentional invariant failure tests as part of this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-22505 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core Feed profiles. It asked for inconsistent profile name/id casing in Bundle-profiles-others.json to be made consistent; the final decision was to leave id values alone but make StructureDefinition.name match the sdf-0 regex name.matches('[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}').
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-22505 was found. R4/R4B release-history profiles-others.xml bundles still show spaced names such as Shareable ActivityDefinition and Provenance Relevant History, while the R5 release-history bundle shows ShareableActivityDefinition and ProvenanceRelevantHistory. The closest source-history application is f87870f3725a6987f2cddcd4d804c6bdf39c0755, a broader FHIR-37449 canonical naming cleanup that changed those profile names to sdf-0-safe PascalCase.
additional_context: The current build no longer has a checked-in Bundle-profiles-others.json source artifact. Current profile source lives in active resource folders governed by source/fhir.ini. Later core cleanup removed or migrated some older shareable/publishable metadata profiles. A full current-source scan found one noncompliant StructureDefinition.name, source/structuredefinition/invariant-tests/cnl-0.f1.fail.xml, but that file is intentionally invalid cnl-0 test data and not a profile source needing correction.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. All 25 current source/**/structuredefinition-profile-*.xml files have names matching the sdf-0-style regex, including representative active names such as DocumentBundle, DefinedParameters, and ProvenanceRelevantHistory.

related_jiras.note: A broad canonical resource name/title cleanup appears to have applied the same sdf-0-safe naming pattern to relevant profile source files, but this reconciliation did not independently decide that issue.
Later cleanup removed several older shareable/publishable profiles from core, reducing the current in-core surface related to the original profiles-others concern.
